messages:
sara_cs: FYI customer reported a big drop in retrieval/reranking quality after yesterday's rollout. they say grounding and citations are missing, recall is lower — examples attached. they're pretty worried because citations were a key part of the contract. :rotating_light:

anya_oncall: can you paste the customer's repro steps and the exact API call they used? also need the model id + rollout timestamp.

sara_cs: pasted below (copied from customer email) — i've redacted PII. they tested staging -> production transition at 2026-03-10 23:10 UTC.

sara_cs: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/retrieve_rerank
-H "Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED]"
-H "Content-Type: application/json"
-d '{
  "query": "treatment options for widget overflow",
  "retriever": {"index": "customer_acme_v1", "k": 50, "score_cutoff": 0.18},
  "reranker": {"model": "reranker-v1.5", "top_k": 5}
}'```

sara_cs: sample response (customer trimmed): ```{"candidates":[], "final_answer":"...references omitted..."}``` they say previous behavior with `reranker-v1.4` returned 5 citations reliably.

mike_eng_ml: interesting — we rolled `reranker-v1.5` to prod as part of the March 10 rollout. that release changed the scoring normalization (softmax temp went from 1.0 -> 1.2) and adjusted the `score_cutoff` recommended default in the SDK docs from 0.15 -> 0.2. could cause fewer returned citations.

javier_prod: that cutoff change was intentional to reduce hallucinated low-confidence citations for other customers. but we should have communicated impact to customers who depend on recall. we did a global rollout?

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-10T22:58Z: rollout reranker-v1.5 -> 100% by canary.

lucy_dataops: i pulled index stats for customer_acme_v1 around the time of the rollout. doc count stable, vector dims unchanged. however similarity distribution shows a small shift: median cosine score dropped ~0.03 after the reranker change (see snippet).

lucy_dataops: ```before: median_sim=0.621
after:  median_sim=0.591
relevant_docs_above_0.2: before=48/50 after=31/50```

norma_support_engineer: quick triage idea: if the reranker now uses a stricter normalization and we increased default `score_cutoff`, customers who passed the SDK default may see fewer results. ask Acme whether they explicitly set `score_cutoff` or used SDK default. if they set 0.18 like in their repro, the new normalization could still push scores below 0.18.

anya_oncall: action items i propose: 1) reproduce with their index snapshot (lucy can we get a short replay using their snapshot + retriever config?), 2) enable debug scoring in prod for this customer for next 24h (log candidate raw scores + reranker logits), 3) if confirmed, roll back reranker to v1.4 for this tenant or adjust recommended defaults, 4) notify the customer with ETA.

mike_eng_ml: i can run an internal A/B: reranker-v1.4 vs v1.5 on the customer's query set (we have their sample prompts) and capture recall/precision and citation presence. i'll do that now and post numbers.

sara_cs: customer says they didn't change anything client-side — they copied the same calls that used to work. they set `score_cutoff` to 0.18 explicitly (see curl).

mike_eng_ml: preliminary A/B (local): on a 120-query sample set: v1.4 recall@5 = 0.87, v1.5 recall@5 = 0.56 ; avg top-k confidence dropped from 0.64 -> 0.58. that's pretty significant. looks correlated with the normalization change. :thinking_face:

javier_prod: we need to weigh the tradeoffs. v1.5 reduced spurious low-confidence citations in other workloads, but for customers that need max recall it's bad. recommendation: add a rollback toggle for tenants (feature flag) and expose reranker normalization param in Console + SDK. also update migration notes.

lucy_dataops: reindex won't help unless we change scoring; this is model-side. But we can simulate raising `k` on retriever or lowering `score_cutoff` to recover recall as a stopgap (customer may accept SDK config change).

norma_support_engineer: i'll draft a customer message offering two options: 1) immediate tenant-level rollback to v1.4 (temporary) OR 2) suggested SDK flags: set `score_cutoff: 0.12` + `reranker.top_k: 10` to try to recover citations. ask which they'd prefer.

anya_oncall: also create a post-rollout regression ticket in ENG-ML with logs + A/B numbers + deploy id (deploy-bot provided timestamp). mike, add the exact diff for normalization change and the tests you ran.

mike_eng_ml: filing JIRA ENG-ML-2481 now and attaching results + a minimal repro.

sara_cs: customer replied — they want immediate rollback for now while we investigate. they mentioned the citations are contractually required.

javier_prod: agree we should prioritize rollback for that tenant. norma, pls coordinate SLA communication. anya, pls approve tenant rollback.

anya_oncall: approved. @deploy-bot can we do a tenant-scoped rollback to reranker-v1.4? include debug logs.

deploy-bot: tenant rollback started for customer_acme_v1 at 2026-03-11T00:15Z. rolling back reranker -> reranker-v1.4.

lucy_dataops: after rollback quick check: recall@5 for customer's sample recovered to 0.85 and citations returned. logs show raw candidate scores unchanged; reranker re-ranked with v1.4 weights and normalized higher.

sara_cs: customer confirmed loss of regression after rollback. they're happy for now but asked for a written postmortem and plan to avoid surprise regressions.

mike_eng_ml: next steps from ENG-ML: (1) revert global normalization change (or make it opt-in), (2) add a retrainer testbench for recall-sensitive customers, (3) surface normalization param in Console and SDK, (4) add automated A/B smoke checks post-rollout for citation metrics. i'll owner ENG-ML-2481.

javier_prod: Product will prepare migration guidance + Console flag. also update rollout playbook to call out recall-sensitive customers.

norma_support_engineer: i'll send the customer an official update and open a follow-up to schedule a runbook review.

anya_oncall: closing this thread — tenant rollback complete and customer stabilized. tagging ENG-ML and Product to follow up. :white_check_mark:
